citation.title: Advances and challenges in KSTAR plasma control toward long-pulse, high-performance experiments
citation.authors: Hahn, S.-h.; Han, H.; Woo, M.H.; et al.

topic: Overview of the KSTAR plasma control system: hardware, magnetic and kinetic control, fault handling and planned upgrades.
own_question: Summarize the KSTAR PCS enhancements and the challenges anticipated for long-pulse operation.
actual_method_and_evidence: This is a descriptive engineering review. It reports a baseline control cycle of 20 kHz and real-time magnetics digitizers at 20 kHz. It describes real-time density feedback and beta_p feedback using the NBI. It reports a feasibility test of electron temperature profile control that used ECE at a 0.5 s control cycle. It mentions SVM and LSTM classifiers for L-H transitions and ELMs. CES, BES, ECEI and ion temperature are not used as real-time inputs.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: The KSTAR PCS was described as running kinetic feedback (density, beta_p) and only a feasibility-level electron temperature profile control that used ECE at a 0.5 s cycle.
claim_checks.qualification: This is the paper's state as of 2018–2020. The temperature control concerns electrons, not impurity ion temperature. It is not evidence about the availability of CES reports.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not relevant to CES. No CES latency or report-arrival information is given.
forbidden_inferences: That KSTAR has a real-time CES or ion-temperature control loop
That a 20 kHz PCS cycle implies our 10 ms computation would be deployable
That this source shows a need for, or benefit of, Ti nowcasting
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Optional as general KSTAR control context only. It provides no evidence on CES, BES/ECEI or nowcasting.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
